Subject: Elevated p99 + intermittent 429s during nightly sync window

Hi Hannah,

We're seeing a recurring spike in p99 (and a handful of 429s) during your 03:00-04:00 UTC maintenance window last night (May 5). Impact appears concentrated on 3 tenant shards (tenant IDs attached in CSV) — their requests queued for several seconds then 429ed. This matches exactly when your background KV-sync job runs. Our checkout throughput dropped ~18% for ~28 minutes (03:12–03:40 UTC).

Can you confirm whether this qualifies as an SLA availability event? If so, please advise on credit calculations (we're a committed Dedicated customer on monthly reserved capacity) and next steps for a postmortem. Attached: tenant-impact-summary-20290505.csv and a small set of request traces.

Thanks,
Sara
Ops Lead, FinApps

Subject: Re: Elevated p99 + intermittent 429s during nightly sync window

Hi all,

Preliminary findings from the node-level trace (attached as kvsync-tail-logs-20290505.gz):
- At 03:11:20 UTC an unanticipated fall-through in the KV-sync backoff logic caused overlapping full-shard writes to a small set of hosts serving tenant shards 7286/8291/8340.
- Write amplification caused per-host write queues to grow; our token-bucket limiter then began rejecting tail requests once queueing exceeded configured burst thresholds — that produced the 429s.
- Total window where queue depth exceeded safe threshold: 03:12:05–03:40:11 UTC (28m 6s). Service continued to accept traffic but saw elevated p95/p99 for affected shards.

Notes on SLO eligibility: the Dedicated contract entitles customers to availability credits where there is a service interruption impacting the total request success above the SLO. This is not a full outage — it is a localized degradation affecting specific tenant shards. Per internal policy we compute a tenant-weighted apportionment of the proportional credit based on request volume for the impacted interval.

I will compile per-tenant request volumes and a proposed credit apportionment by EOD (PST). For transparency I’ve included the raw node traces in the attachment.

Diego
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: kvsync-tail-logs-20290505.gz (type: application/gzip, 2.1MB)

Date: 2029-05-06T09:12:07Z
Subject: Re: Request: tenant-weighted apportionment & credit eligibility after KV-sync throttling

Sara — thanks for the patience. Diego and I reviewed the traces and the per-tenant volumes. Summary and ask below.

Summary of verification:
- Impact window verified: 2029-05-05 03:12:05–03:40:11 UTC.
- Affected tenants: 7286, 8291, 8340 (matches your CSV).
- Measured request success delta vs baseline across the window: tenant 7286: -24% success, tenant 8291: -15%, tenant 8340: -7%.
- Incident root cause: overlapping KV-sync writes due to a race in the backoff reset path; caused write queue growth and subsequent token-bucket rejections on a subset of hosts.

Credit path and ask:
- Eligibility: This qualifies as a partial degradation event under Section 4.2. We will calculate a proportional credit pro-rated by tenant-weighted request volume over the impacted interval.
- Proposed apportionment method: use per-tenant request counts during 03:12–03:40 to weight the total credit pool. Our default is tenant-volume weighting unless you prefer equal-split or contract-specified carve-outs.
- To finalize: please confirm you accept tenant-volume weighting, and whether you'd like the credit as a one-time invoice credit or as a recurring monthly credit applied across the next three invoices.

Postmortem and remediation:
- We will schedule a 60-minute postmortem with SRE, Product, and your ops team (requested times: May 8 15:00 UTC or May 9 09:00 UTC).
- Immediate remediation: roll a fix to the backoff reset logic and add a canary to the background job to prevent overlapping full-shard writes. Deploy ETA: May 7 02:00 UTC.

Attachments included: kvsync-tail-logs-20290505.gz (raw traces), tenant-impact-summary-20290505.csv (your CSV with matched request counts).

If that plan looks good I’ll produce the formal credit calculation and a DocuSign amendment if you want the credit applied to invoice rather than account balance. Laura — can you prep the two credit options for FinApps?

Thanks,
Hannah
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
